curation.lead:
Knightsbridge Capital Partners Holding I, II, and III SA are three parallel Luxembourg sociétés anonymes registered with the Luxembourg Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés as B279238, B280404, and B281581, all incorporated within a three-month window between August and October 2023 [Finding #11219]. Each of the three vehicles shares an identical scaffold: registered office at 2 rue Sainte-Zithe, L-2763 Luxembourg; sole director Mathieu Villaume; auditor JNP Audit Services; and EUR 30,000 share capital [Finding #11219]. Holding II was registered on 21 September 2023 with formation dated 31 August 2023, and Holding III was registered on 17 October 2023 [Finding #11219].

The structural uniformity across the trio is consistent with a special-purpose-vehicle-per-investment pattern typical of private-equity fund deal-by-deal architecture, though Ithildin synthesis from registry filings cannot directly observe the underlying mandate [Finding #11219]. The 2 rue Sainte-Zithe domicile sits on the same Luxembourg street as Rothschild & Co Luxembourg's office, which forms the basis for an Ithildin inference that the trio is Rothschild-adjacent; this remains an inference, not a confirmed beneficial-ownership link [Finding #11219]. The trio is domiciled away from 12 rue Guillaume Schneider, the NeoTrust Fiduciary address that hosts Villaume's earlier SPQR Capital Holding SA and Compagnie Du Saleve SA directorships [Finding #11219].

The Lux trio is distinct from the unrelated UK entity Knightsbridge Capital Partners Ltd (UK Companies House CO# 11314526), which was incorporated 17 April 2018 and dissolved 26 January 2021, with only directors Luke Hexter and Fatima Leitao on record and zero officer overlap with the Wind Hellas, SPQR, Compagnie Du Saleve, or Five Arrows rosters [Finding #11217]. The 2.5-year gap between the UK entity's January 2021 dissolution and the Lux trio's August-October 2023 formation, combined with disjoint directorships, supports the Ithildin assessment that the shared 'Knightsbridge' name is nominal reuse rather than corporate continuity [Finding #11217].
curation.system_role: The Knightsbridge Lux trio is a three-vehicle Luxembourg holding scaffold whose existence anchors the Round 6 disambiguation: it shows how distinct corporate-administration ecosystems can share a brand-name but no operational substance, while a single fiduciary (Villaume) extends an established Lux mandate into a new, Rothschild-street domicile.

sections.title: Corporate Structure
sections.content: The three Knightsbridge Lux SPVs are sociétés anonymes registered with the Luxembourg RCS at numbers B279238 (Holding I), B280404 (Holding II), and B281581 (Holding III) [Finding #11219]. All three were formed inside a three-month window in the second half of 2023, with Holding II registered on 21 September 2023 against a formation date of 31 August 2023, and Holding III registered on 17 October 2023 [Finding #11219]. Each SA is capitalised at EUR 30,000, the Lux statutory minimum for the SA form [Finding #11219]. Each is audited by JNP Audit Services, and each lists Mathieu Villaume as the sole director [Finding #11219]. The replicated scaffold across three separately numbered RCS entries, formed in close sequence, is the surface signature of a SPV-per-investment pattern typical of private-equity deal-by-deal vehicles, though Ithildin analysis of registry filings alone does not establish the underlying investment mandate [Finding #11219].

sections.title: Luxembourg Domicile and the Rothschild Street
sections.content: All three SPVs share the registered office at 2 rue Sainte-Zithe, L-2763 Luxembourg [Finding #11219]. Rothschild & Co Luxembourg lists its own office on the same street, per the firm's own published offices listing, and Ithildin synthesis treats the shared street address as a strong inference that the trio sits in the Rothschild-adjacent Luxembourg cluster [Finding #11219]. The inference is structural rather than ownership-confirmed; registry filings disclose the registered office but do not name the beneficial owner, and Rothschild & Co's role here is not directly recorded in the Knightsbridge filings examined [Finding #11219]. The 2 rue Sainte-Zithe address is distinct from 12 rue Guillaume Schneider L-2522, the NeoTrust Fiduciary domicile that hosts SPQR Capital Holding SA and Compagnie Du Saleve SA, where Villaume also serves as director [Finding #11219]. The change of domiciliation between Villaume's earlier Lux mandates and the 2023 Knightsbridge trio is an evidence point in its own right: the same fiduciary moved into a different administrative ecosystem within the same jurisdiction.

sections.title: Disambiguation from the UK Entity
sections.content: The Lux Knightsbridge trio is not corporately related to Knightsbridge Capital Partners Ltd, the UK entity registered at Companies House under number 11314526 [Finding #11217]. The UK company was incorporated on 17 April 2018 at 33 St James's Square, London SW1Y 4JS, and dissolved on 26 January 2021 [Finding #11217]. Its only recorded directors are Luke Hexter (DOB February 1989, British), who served as director from 17 April 2018 and as secretary between 17 April 2018 and 11 August 2018, and Fatima Leitao (DOB May 1964, British), who became a director on 8 August 2018 [Finding #11217]. Cross-checking against the broader Lux roster examined in Round 6 — Bertrand G. des Pallieres, Mathieu Villaume, Alessandro Benedetti, the Marchiolo and Brachetti circles, and the Wind Hellas creditor ring — produced zero overlapping officers [Finding #11217]. The 2.5-year gap between the UK dissolution in January 2021 and the Lux trio's formation between August and October 2023, combined with the disjoint directorships, supports the Ithildin position that the shared 'Knightsbridge Capital Partners' label is nominal name reuse rather than evidence of continuity [Finding #11217].

sections.title: Significance to the Investigation
sections.content: The trio's investigative significance turns on Villaume's mandate rather than on observed transactions, because the 2023-vintage SPVs have not yet generated the kind of audited annual filings that would expose counterparties or transferred assets [Finding #11219]. Villaume already directs Compagnie Du Saleve SA (Lux B223232), owned by Five Arrows AutoBench Holding Sarl, the private-equity arm of Rothschild & Co; that prior link is the first documented Villaume-Rothschild intersection on the public record [Finding #11129]. The Knightsbridge trio's domiciliation on the same Luxembourg street as Rothschild & Co Luxembourg, combined with Villaume's existing Five-Arrows-orbit directorship at Compagnie Du Saleve, leads to an Ithildin synthesis hypothesis that the 2023 Knightsbridge mandate extends an established Villaume-Rothschild administrative relationship into a new SPV cluster; analysis of the registry filings indicates this remains an inference rather than a confirmed beneficial-ownership link [Finding #11219][Finding #11166]. Cross-reference of registry filings indicates Villaume operates as a cross-jurisdiction corporate-administration custodian whose mandate-portability across REYL & Cie, Alter Domus, IQ-EQ, Fundcraft, and Vault Administration / Azur & Partners spans roughly 155 director reports and 84 or more appointments across the UK, Luxembourg, and Malta; Ithildin synthesis treats this volume of mandates as load-bearing evidence of a personal-relationship fiduciary role rather than passive nominee status [Finding #11129]. The Knightsbridge trio is the most recent observed extension of that mandate. The structural picture is therefore: a single fiduciary, a deliberate move to a new Lux administrative ecosystem, and a triplet of SPVs whose deal-by-deal architecture is typical of private-equity vehicles but whose underlying mandate, counterparties, and beneficial owners are not yet observable in the registry record [Finding #11219].

open_questions: What investment mandate sits behind the Holding I, II, and III split — is each SPV tied to a distinct portfolio company or asset, as the deal-by-deal pattern would suggest, and which mandate sequencing produced the August-October 2023 formation cadence?
Does Rothschild & Co Luxembourg or any Five Arrows fund vehicle hold record or beneficial ownership in any of B279238, B280404, or B281581, beyond the 2 rue Sainte-Zithe street-adjacency inference?

Are there annual accounts, share-pledge filings, or Lux RCS publications dated 2024 or 2025 that disclose counterparties, asset transfers, or financing structures associated with the three Knightsbridge SPVs?
Does JNP Audit Services audit other Villaume-directed Lux SAs, and does that auditor relationship trace to the same Rothschild-adjacent administrative cluster or to a separate ecosystem?
Has any of the three SPVs filed share-capital increases, bond issuances, or pledge agreements that would identify lenders or co-investors after the 2023 incorporation?
